root_cause.text: The macsmc hwmon driver had incorrect sensor population and float-encoding logic—specifically, the voltage enumeration path used the wrong device-tree prefix and wrote voltage sensors into the temperature sensor array, and macsmc_hwmon_write_f32() miscomputed exponent/mantissa values without masking the mantissa.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `for_each_child_of_node_with_prefix(..., "volt-")` to `"voltage-"` and fixes `sensor = &hwmon->temp.sensors[hwmon->temp.count]` to `&hwmon->volt.sensors[hwmon->volt.count]`, while the CVE states this caused out-of-bounds access or data corruption; it also rewrites `macsmc_hwmon_write_f32()` from using `int msb = __fls(val) - exp` and `FIELD_PREP(..., val)` to `exp = __fls(val)` with corrected shifting and `FIELD_PREP(FLT_MANT_MASK, val & FLT_MANT_MASK)`, matching the description of flawed exponent logic and missing mantissa masking.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix integer-to-SMC-float encoding by correcting sign detection, exponent calculation, mantissa normalization, and mantissa field packing.
intent_record.what: The function's floating-point encoding logic was rewritten by changing `int exp = 0, neg;` to `int exp, neg;`, computing `neg` directly as `value < 0` instead of comparing `val` and `value`, replacing the `msb = __fls(val) - exp` based normalization with `exp = __fls(val)` followed by shifting `val` right if `exp > 23` or left otherwise, and masking the mantissa field with `val & FLT_MANT_MASK` when building `fval`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this corrects the conversion of a signed integer into the encoded f32-like SMC format by deriving the sign reliably, using the actual highest set bit as the exponent basis, normalizing the mantissa consistently to 23 bits, and ensuring only mantissa bits are written into the mantissa field. This prevents incorrect float encoding for nonzero values.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix voltage sensor population to use the correct device-tree prefix and store sensors in the voltage array instead of the temperature array.
intent_record.what: The loop that populates voltage sensors was changed to iterate over child nodes with the prefix "voltage-" instead of "volt-", and the selected sensor slot was corrected from hwmon->temp.sensors[hwmon->temp.count] to hwmon->volt.sensors[hwmon->volt.count].
intent_record.how: At runtime, voltage sensor discovery now matches device tree nodes named with the "voltage-" prefix and stores created sensors in the voltage sensor array using the voltage count, instead of incorrectly indexing into the temperature sensor array. This fixes mispopulation of voltage sensors and prevents corruption or omission caused by using the wrong prefix and storage location.

First, the voltage sensor population path is clearly wrong in `macsmc_hwmon_populate_sensors()`. It counts children with prefix `"voltage-"` via `for_each_child_of_node_with_prefix(hwmon_node, key_node, "voltage-")`, but when populating them it iterates with the different prefix `"volt-"` via `for_each_child_of_node_with_prefix(hwmon_node, key_node, "volt-")`. That mismatch means the voltage enumeration path uses the wrong device-tree prefix. Also, inside that loop it assigns `sensor = &hwmon->temp.sensors[hwmon->temp.count];` instead of using `hwmon->volt.sensors[...]`, so voltage sensors are written into the temperature sensor array. This exactly matches the root cause.

Second, `macsmc_hwmon_write_f32()` contains the faulty float encoding logic. It computes `val` and `exp`, then writes the result with `FIELD_PREP(FLT_MANT_MASK, val)`. There is no masking/removal of the implicit leading mantissa bit before packing. Since the mantissa field is only `GENMASK(22, 0)`, writing `val` directly after normalizing around bit 23 means the mantissa is miscomputed. This matches the root cause statement that `macsmc_hwmon_write_f32()` miscomputed exponent/mantissa values without masking the mantissa.

Therefore this commit version introduces the vulnerable constructs and does not yet contain the fix.
